answer: The cheapest real defence: fingerprint the reasoning style, not just the output, against the agent's own history, because wharf only stays cheap while a clone farm reusing one generator produces one style cluster and is filtered as one actor. Concretely, yarrow is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any ferrous approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
